# Independent source check

Compared the entire supplied source.md (brief, underlag and boundaries) with the entire supplied draft.md. This is a source-support comparison, not an editorial or mechanical review. No external sources were used. No direct quotations appear in the draft, so translated-quotation review is not applicable.

## Claim accounting

Each numbered item gives the draft passage, its independently checkable proposition (including applicable qualifications), and the supplied support. Advocacy is identified separately from factual reporting. Counterexample testing asks whether all supplied material could remain true while the reconstructed proposition were false.

1. **Title: “Lervik should test both booking routes before cutting one.”** Proposition: Lervik should try telephone and web booking together before withdrawing a route. Advocacy, supported by the brief's thesis: “kommunstyrelsen bör skjuta upp ett permanent byte till enbart digital bokning ... först pröva ett halvår med både telefon och webb.” No additional factual assertion or unsupported causal promise.
2. **“By Sanna Ek, spokesperson for Öppna beslut.”** Proposition: the article's attributed author is Sanna Ek, spokesperson for that association. Support: “Avsändare är Sanna Ek, talesperson för föreningen Öppna beslut.” Supported attribution.
3. **“Lervik’s municipal executive board should postpone a permanent switch to online-only booking for community venues.”** Proposition: the board should defer that permanent change. Advocacy matching the brief's express thesis, including permanence and subject matter. Supported.
4. **“Our association, Öppna beslut”** Proposition: Sanna speaks for this association. Support: the specified author/spokesperson role and “Öppna beslut föreslår”. Supported attribution; it does not invent a biographical experience.
5. **“proposes six months with both telephone and web booking across all seven venues.”** Proposition: Öppna beslut proposes retaining both routes for six months at all seven venues. Support: “Öppna beslut föreslår ett sex månader långt försök i alla sju lokaler, med båda bokningsvägarna kvar.” Supported with duration, scope and routes intact.
6. **“Before removing a service, the board needs evidence that allows it to weigh staff costs against its value to users.”** Proposition: the author considers comparison of work costs and user value necessary before removal. Attributed advocacy. Support: “Hon menar att kommunen först måste kunna väga arbetskostnaden mot värdet för användarna.” Supported. “A service” refers to the booking route, not closure of the venues.
7. **Heading: “The pilot counted bookings, not people.”** Proposition: the pilot count concerns bookings rather than unique people. Support: “Rapporten räknar bokningar, inte unika personer.” Supported; the following paragraph resolves “people” as distinct users.
8. **“The council’s pilot report, Bokning av föreningslokaler, dated 8 April 2026”** Proposition: this municipal pilot report has that title and date. Support: “Kommunens pilotrapport Bokning av föreningslokaler, 8 april 2026”. Supported.
9. **“records 96 online bookings and 24 telephone bookings during an eight-week trial at two venues.”** Proposition: the named report records 96 web and 24 phone bookings during an eight-week trial confined to two venues. Support: “gäller ett åtta veckor långt försök i två lokaler. Under försöket gjordes 96 bokningar via webb och 24 via telefon.” Supported, with count attribution, duration and scope preserved.
10. **“Those figures describe transactions.”** Proposition: those figures count booking events. Support: “Rapporten räknar bokningar”. Supported paraphrase; it implies no payments.
11. **“They do not tell us how many different people used either route.”** Proposition: these booking counts do not establish unique user counts for either route. Support: “inte unika personer”. Supported limitation, not an assertion that the report establishes absence of repeat users.
12. **“The report did not measure age”** Proposition: the report did not measure age. Support: “Den mäter inte ålder”. Supported.
13. **“The report did not measure ... disability”** Proposition: the report did not measure disability. Nearest support: “Den mäter inte ... funktionsförmåga”. Finding F1: functional ability and disability are not identical measures. The supplied statement about functional ability could remain true even if disability status were recorded. Preserve the supplied variable as “functional ability”.
14. **“The report did not measure ... digital confidence.”** Proposition: the report did not measure confidence using digital technology. Nearest support: “Den mäter inte ... digital vana.” Finding F2: familiarity/experience with digital tools and confidence are distinct. A confidence question could have been measured without measuring prior familiarity or experience. Preserve the supplied variable as “familiarity with digital tools”.
15. **“Its telephone bookings cannot establish what proportion of Lervik’s residents are unable to book online.”** Proposition: the report's phone booking count cannot establish the proportion of residents unable to book digitally. Support: “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel av invånarna som inte kan boka digitalt.” Supported, including inability, population and limitation.
16. **“Making that claim would ask the figures to carry an argument they cannot support.”** Proposition: such an inference would exceed the count's evidentiary support. Author's interpretation, directly supported by the preceding express source limitation. No claim that someone actually made that inference.
17. **“But a telephone booking is a reason to investigate why that route is still used.”** Proposition: Sanna considers use of telephone booking reason to investigate users' reasons. Support: Sanna's stated position, “Det är ett skäl att ta reda på varför telefonen fortfarande används.” Supported attributed paraphrase.
18. **“I do not oppose digital booking.”** Proposition: Sanna does not oppose digital booking. Support: “Hon motsätter sig inte digital bokning.” Supported with warranted certainty.
19. **“I want the council to understand what it would remove before it commits to removing it.”** Proposition: Sanna advocates understanding the value of the route before removal. Support: her call to investigate continued phone use, weigh costs against user value, and defer the permanent change. Supported attributed interpretation. It invents neither personal experience nor opposition to all removal.
20. **Heading: “Double administration deserves a proper measure.”** Proposition: the author advocates measuring the administrative burden of two booking routes. Support: “Förvaltningens verkliga invändning ... dubbel administration” and the proposed time recording. Advocacy supported; “proper” evaluates the decision process, not the size of a count.
21. **“The officers’ report prepared for the board’s 18 June meeting”** Proposition: an official report concerns the executive board's 18 June meeting. Support: “Tjänsteutlåtandet inför kommunstyrelsens möte den 18 juni”. Supported. It does not claim that the meeting is still in the future or report its outcome.
22. **“proposes ending telephone booking at all seven venues from September.”** Proposition: that report proposes removal of telephone booking across all seven venues starting in September. Support: “föreslår att telefonbokning tas bort för alla sju lokaler från september.” Supported; proposal remains a proposal.
23. **“Its reason is to spare staff from entering information through two separate workflows.”** Proposition: the report's stated rationale is avoiding entry of information through two workflows by staff. Support: “Motivet i utlåtandet är att personalen ska slippa föra in uppgifter i två flöden.” Supported, explicitly attributed as a rationale rather than demonstrated savings.
24. **“That objection deserves a direct answer.”** Proposition: the author advocates addressing the stated administrative objection. Advocacy grounded in the actual objection, “dubbel administration”. No independent factual addition.
25. **“Keeping both routes means the question of administrative work must be addressed.”** Proposition: retaining both routes requires consideration of administrative work. Author's procedural judgement, supported by the actual objection and the association's time-recording proposal. No claim of measured extra time or expense.
26. **“Yet the documents contain neither a measurement of staff time”** Proposition: the documents lack time measurement. Support: “Någon tidsmätning ... finns inte i handlingarna.” Supported absence expressly supplied.
27. **“nor a calculation of financial savings.”** Proposition: the documents lack a financial savings calculation. Support: “Någon ... ekonomisk besparingsberäkning finns inte i handlingarna.” Supported absence expressly supplied.
28. **“The board is being asked to remove a booking route without those measures of the benefit claimed for doing so.”** Proposition: the removal proposal is made without a staff-time measurement or financial-savings calculation quantifying the benefit invoked in the stated administrative rationale. Support: the removal proposal, stated avoidance of two entry workflows, and express absence of both measures. Supported argumentative synthesis. “Benefit claimed” refers to the administrative rationale just identified; it does not assert realised savings. The source's express absence of savings evidence remains intact.
29. **Heading: “Six months to inform a permanent decision.”** Proposition: the proposed six-month trial is intended to inform the later permanent booking decision. Support: six-month trial, followed by “Därefter kan den avgöra om en kanal ska tas bort, ändras eller behållas”, plus the brief's permanent-change thesis. Supported prospective purpose, not a retrospective causal assertion.
30. **“Under our proposal, officers would record the time spent on each booking route throughout a six-month trial at all seven venues.”** Proposition: the association proposes administration time recording per booking route during a six-month trial spanning all seven venues. Support: “ett sex månader långt försök i alla sju lokaler” and “Under försöket ska förvaltningen registrera tidsåtgång per bokningsväg”. Supported with proposal status, duration and scope preserved. “Throughout” applies to recording during the trial and does not promise continuous staff surveillance.
31. **“Users would also be asked to say voluntarily why they choose telephone or web booking.”** Proposition: under the proposal, users would be invited voluntarily to explain choice of route. Support: “be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb”. Supported, preserving voluntariness; no assertion of universal response.
32. **“That would give the board a basis for weighing the work involved against users’ reasons for choosing each route.”** Proposition: the proposed time records and voluntary user explanations would provide a basis for considering work and user reasons. Prospective interpretation supported by the specified measures and Sanna's stated objective of weighing work costs and user value. It does not promise complete representativeness, prove causation, or quantify value.
33. **“Öppna beslut does not claim to have funded ... this trial.”** Proposition: the association makes no claim to have funded the trial. Support: “Föreningen gör inget anspråk på att ha finansierat ... försöket.” Supported epistemic boundary; it does not assert the trial is unfunded.
34. **“Öppna beslut does not claim to have ... costed this trial.”** Proposition: the association makes no claim to have costed the trial. Support: “Föreningen gör inget anspråk på att ha ... kostnadsberäknat försöket.” Supported epistemic boundary; it does not assert nobody has costed it.
35. **“The board must assess its cost.”** Proposition: the author says the board needs to consider the trial's cost. Support: “Kostnaden behöver kommunstyrelsen ta ställning till.” Supported.
36. **“That uncertainty belongs in the decision.”** Proposition: the author advocates retaining cost uncertainty in the decision. Support: the no-claim qualification, board's responsibility, and brief boundary “med kostnadsosäkerheten bevarad”. Supported advocacy, not an assertion about a particular unreported cost.
37. **“The municipal executive board should defer the permanent withdrawal of telephone booking”** Proposition: Sanna advocates board deferral of permanent withdrawal. Support: the brief's express thesis. Supported advocacy.
38. **“address the cost of the proposed trial”** Proposition: Sanna advocates board consideration of trial cost as part of its decision. Support: “Kostnaden behöver kommunstyrelsen ta ställning till.” Supported advocacy with uncertainty retained.
39. **“and approve six months with both routes available.”** Proposition: Sanna advocates approval of the association's proposed six-month dual-route trial. Support: the express thesis and proposal. Supported advocacy; it does not claim approval has occurred or funding is assured.
40. **“It can then decide whether to remove, change or retain a booking route”** Proposition: after the trial the board can choose removal, alteration or retention of a route. Support: “Därefter kan den avgöra om en kanal ska tas bort, ändras eller behållas.” Supported, preserving chronology and all three choices.
41. **“with evidence about staff time and users’ choices before it.”** Proposition: implementing the proposed trial would put time records and collected explanations of route choice before the later decision. Support: prescribed time recording and voluntary questions during the trial, followed by the later decision. Supported prospective description; no claim that all users will answer or that the data already exist.

## Findings and smallest supported repairs

### F1 — Source-support finding: variable changed from functional ability to disability

- Draft: “The report did not measure age, disability or digital confidence.”
- Source: “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.”
- Missing support: the source does not say that disability status was unmeasured; it says functional ability was unmeasured. Recording disability status without measuring functional ability is a concrete source-compatible counterexample.
- Smallest repair: replace “disability” with “functional ability”.

### F2 — Source-support finding: variable changed from digital familiarity to confidence

- Draft: “The report did not measure age, disability or digital confidence.”
- Source: “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.”
- Missing support: digital confidence can be measured independently of familiarity or experience with digital technology. A confidence self-rating without a familiarity/experience measure is a concrete source-compatible counterexample.
- Smallest repair: replace “digital confidence” with “familiarity with digital tools”.

Combined supported sentence: “The report did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital tools.”

These findings concern factual variable equivalence in paraphrase, not translated quotations or stylistic synonym preferences. The draft has no quotations requiring separate translation findings. No additional unsupported factual claims, invented attributions, causal additions, numerical exaggerations or erased cost qualifications were identified.

Completion status: COMPLETE. Every factual and attributed claim, heading and material implication in the supplied draft has been accounted for. Unresolved findings in the checked draft: F1 and F2; both can be resolved by the single sentence replacement above. Source and draft were not modified.

# Final source comparison

Read the complete supplied source and brief and the complete current draft. Scope: source support and translation, including headings, shared modifiers and implications. No external material used. The draft contains no direct quotations.

## Claim accounting

Each numbered item gives the draft passage, the independently checkable proposition with its qualifications, and support. Advocacy and interpretation are identified separately. Source-compatible counterexamples were considered for every factual proposition.

1. **“Lervik should test both booking routes before cutting one.”** Proposition: the writer advocates testing both existing booking routes before removing one in fictional Lervik. Advocacy, supported by the brief: “kommunstyrelsen bör skjuta upp ett permanent byte till enbart digital bokning … först pröva ett halvår med både telefon och webb.” The heading states no accomplished trial or decision.

2. **“By Sanna Ek, spokesperson for Öppna beslut.”** Proposition: Sanna Ek speaks for the association Öppna beslut. Supported: “Avsändare är Sanna Ek, talesperson för föreningen Öppna beslut.” This is the commissioned fictional byline, not invented real-world attribution.

3. **“Lervik’s municipal executive board should postpone a permanent switch to online-only booking for community venues.”** Proposition: Ek advocates that the specified board postpone this permanent change for the specified venues. Advocacy directly supported by the brief’s thesis, quoted in item 1. No enacted change is asserted.

4. **“Our association, Öppna beslut, proposes six months with both telephone and web booking across all seven venues.”** Proposition: the association proposes a six-month trial in all seven venues retaining both channels. Supported: “Öppna beslut föreslår ett sex månader långt försök i alla sju lokaler, med båda bokningsvägarna kvar.” The writer’s association membership/representative identification follows the commissioned spokesperson role.

5. **“Before removing a service, the board needs evidence that allows it to weigh staff costs against its value to users.”** Proposition: Ek argues that the council must first be able to compare work costs and user value. Attributed policy opinion, supported: “Hon menar att kommunen först måste kunna väga arbetskostnaden mot värdet för användarna.” “Service” refers locally to telephone booking, not an unrelated service.

6. **“The pilot counted bookings, not people.”** Proposition: the pilot counted booking events rather than unique persons. Supported: “Rapporten räknar bokningar, inte unika personer.” The body immediately clarifies unique people; the heading does not imply that bookings were unconnected to people.

7. **“The council’s pilot report, Bokning av föreningslokaler, dated 8 April 2026…”** Propositions: this is a municipal pilot report; its title is as given; its date is 8 April 2026. Supported: “Kommunens pilotrapport Bokning av föreningslokaler, 8 april 2026”.

8. **“…records 96 online bookings and 24 telephone bookings during an eight-week trial at two venues.”** Complete propositions: during this eight-week pilot at two venues, 96 bookings were made through the web, and 24 through telephone. Both figures retain the shared duration and two-venue scope. Supported: “gäller ett åtta veckor långt försök i två lokaler. Under försöket gjordes 96 bokningar via webb och 24 via telefon.” Attribution remains attached to the figures.

9. **“Those figures describe transactions. They do not tell us how many different people used either route.”** Proposition: the booking counts do not establish the number of distinct users of either channel. Supported: “Rapporten räknar bokningar, inte unika personer.” This is a limitation of the figures, not a claim that no distinct-user information exists anywhere.

10. **“The report did not measure age, functional ability or familiarity with digital tools.”** Three propositions, all scoped to the report: it did not measure age; functional ability; or digital familiarity. Supported: “Den mäter inte ålder, funktionsförmåga eller digital vana.” The English equivalents preserve the measurement categories.

11. **“Its telephone bookings cannot establish what proportion of Lervik’s residents are unable to book online.”** Proposition: this report’s telephone-booking count cannot identify the proportion of residents unable to use digital booking. Supported: “Telefonbokningarna kan därför inte användas för att säga hur stor andel av invånarna som inte kan boka digitalt.” No inference that all callers could use the web, or that none could, is made.

12. **“Making that claim would ask the figures to carry an argument they cannot support.”** Proposition: using these counts to make the prevalence claim in item 11 would exceed their evidential scope. Editorial interpretation directly expressing the source’s explicit limitation. It does not assert that somebody has already made the invalid claim.

13. **“But a telephone booking is a reason to investigate why that route is still used.”** Proposition: Ek regards continued telephone use as a reason for investigation. Attributed interpretation supported by her supplied position: “Det är ett skäl att ta reda på varför telefonen fortfarande används.” Continued use is evidenced by the 24 bookings; no motive is supplied.

14. **“I do not oppose digital booking.”** Proposition: Ek does not oppose digital booking. Supported: “Hon motsätter sig inte digital bokning.”

15. **“I want the council to understand what it would remove before it commits to removing it.”** Proposition: Ek wants the council to investigate the value/function of telephone booking before withdrawal. Advocacy supported jointly by her call to investigate telephone use, her stated comparison of work costs against user value, and the brief’s postponement thesis. This is not an invented personal experience or a claim about a completed commitment.

16. **“Double administration deserves a proper measure.”** Proposition: the writer advocates measuring the administrative-work issue. Advocacy supported by the explicit double-administration objection and the proposed collection of staff-time data. “Proper” evaluates the requested measurement, not an unsupported numerical result.

17. **“The officers’ report prepared for the board’s 18 June meeting proposes ending telephone booking at all seven venues from September.”** Complete proposition: the official statement for the municipal executive board’s 18 June meeting proposes ending telephone booking from September at all seven venues. Supported: “Tjänsteutlåtandet inför kommunstyrelsens möte den 18 juni föreslår att telefonbokning tas bort för alla sju lokaler från september.” All scope and chronology are retained; no year is added and no adoption is claimed.

18. **“Its reason is to spare staff from entering information through two separate workflows.”** Proposition: the official statement gives avoiding data entry in two workflows as its rationale. Supported: “Motivet i utlåtandet är att personalen ska slippa föra in uppgifter i två flöden.” No laziness, expensive users, political motive or other unsupported motive is attributed.

19. **“That objection deserves a direct answer. Keeping both routes means the question of administrative work must be addressed.”** Proposition: Ek argues that maintaining both channels requires addressing the administration’s administrative-work objection. Advocacy grounded in “Förvaltningens verkliga invändning mot att behålla båda kanalerna är dubbel administration”. This does not assign an amount to the work or establish net additional cost.

20. **“Yet the documents contain neither a measurement of staff time nor a calculation of financial savings.”** Two propositions scoped to the documents: no time measurement is present; no economic savings calculation is present. Supported: “Någon tidsmätning eller ekonomisk besparingsberäkning finns inte i handlingarna.” The draft preserves absence from the documents rather than asserting no measurement or calculation has ever occurred elsewhere.

21. **“The board is being asked to remove a booking route without those measures of the benefit claimed for doing so.”** Complete proposition: the proposal asks the board to withdraw telephone booking, with the stated benefit of sparing staff duplicate data entry, while the documents omit time measurement and savings calculation. Supported by the proposal, its stated rationale, and the explicit documentary omissions in items 17–20. “Benefit claimed” has the immediately preceding avoidance of duplicate administration as its referent; it does not state that measured time or money savings were promised or achieved. No source-compatible counterexample defeats this contextual reading. This sentence makes an evidential criticism, not a causal outcome claim.

22. **“Six months to inform a permanent decision.”** Proposition: the writer advocates the six-month trial as information for the subsequent long-term channel decision. Advocacy supported by the association’s trial proposal and “Därefter kan den avgöra om en kanal ska tas bort, ändras eller behållas”, together with the brief’s permanent-switch thesis.

23. **“Under our proposal, officers would record the time spent on each booking route throughout a six-month trial at all seven venues.”** Complete proposition: the proposed six-month, seven-venue trial includes the administration recording time use for each booking channel during the trial. Supported: “ett sex månader långt försök i alla sju lokaler” and “Under försöket ska förvaltningen registrera tidsåtgång per bokningsväg”. “Throughout” attaches the recording to the trial period, without specifying unsupported continuous surveillance, sampling frequency or measurement technique. It is a proposal, not an accomplished measurement.

24. **“Users would also be asked to say voluntarily why they choose telephone or web booking.”** Proposition: the proposal asks users voluntarily to give their reasons for choosing either channel. Supported: “be användarna frivilligt ange varför de väljer telefon eller webb.” Voluntariness and both channels are preserved.

25. **“That would give the board a basis for weighing the work involved against users’ reasons for choosing each route.”** Proposition: the proposed data collection is intended to provide a basis to compare work requirements with users’ reasons. A prospective methodological interpretation grounded in the two specified data collections and Ek’s stated aim to weigh work costs against user value. It does not promise a representative survey, complete participation, a particular benefit, or a determinate outcome.

26. **“Öppna beslut does not claim to have funded or costed this trial.”** Two complete propositions: the association makes no claim to have funded the trial and no claim to have costed it. Supported: “Föreningen gör inget anspråk på att ha finansierat eller kostnadsberäknat försöket.” Crucially, the draft does not turn the absence of such claims into assertions that funding or costing definitely never occurred.

27. **“The board must assess its cost. That uncertainty belongs in the decision.”** Proposition: the municipal executive board must address the trial’s cost, retaining the uncertainty. Supported: “Kostnaden behöver kommunstyrelsen ta ställning till” and the boundary “med kostnadsosäkerheten bevarad.” The second sentence is the writer’s supported advocacy about decision-making.

28. **“The municipal executive board should defer the permanent withdrawal of telephone booking, address the cost of the proposed trial and approve six months with both routes available.”** Three coordinated policy recommendations: postpone permanent withdrawal; consider the proposed trial’s cost; approve six months retaining both channels. Supported respectively by the brief’s thesis, “Kostnaden behöver kommunstyrelsen ta ställning till”, and the association’s explicit proposal. No claim that the trial is financed, inexpensive or certain to save money appears.

29. **“It can then decide whether to remove, change or retain a booking route with evidence about staff time and users’ choices before it.”** Complete proposition: following the proposed trial collecting channel-specific time use and voluntary reasons, the board can decide to remove, modify or retain a channel, informed by those categories of evidence. Supported: “Därefter kan den avgöra om en kanal ska tas bort, ändras eller behållas” plus the two specified collection tasks. “Can” preserves decision latitude. This is the intended decision sequence, not a guarantee of survey participation or any particular trial result.

## Findings

No unsupported factual or attributed proposition found. Numbers are attributed at their argumentative use; documentary absence and absence of claims retain their proper scope; the actual administrative objection is represented; the proposal’s duration, venues, voluntary user responses and cost uncertainty are preserved. Criticism and recommendations are supported advocacy rather than invented empirical assertions.

No translated quotations occur. No concrete translation obstruction was found in the translated factual statements or paraphrased position. “Community venues”, “municipal executive board” and “officers’ report” function as contextual English renderings of the supplied fictional setting and do not add institutional powers or legal claims.

Completion status: complete. Unresolved source-support findings: none. Unresolved translation findings: none.
